why_relevant: Consumer finance portal with structured reference data (bank codes, list of banks) and explainer journalism on operational shifts such as cashless branches ('bezhotovostne pobocky', end of teller counters) — a leading indicator for cash-handling and self-service hardware demand.

Newly discovered specialist SK financial-sector trade title with a dedicated banks & insurers desk; observed publishing sector-wide technology round-ups (AI assistants, virtual bankers, new investment platforms across SK banks/insurers in 2026). Round-ups like this are high-yield for vendor/partnership mapping.
SK-language fintech/technology news site with a Technologie category; covers mobile-banking trends and fintech-bank tie-ups in Slovak. Complements the English trade press for local vendor names.

Global bank-tech trade press; confirmed SK-relevant items (Erste Group's George PSD2 platform launch in Slovakia; FinTech Hub Slovakia formed by Slovak Fintech Association, Mastercard and Vacuumlabs). Press-release section names vendors banks themselves downplay.

source_subtype: international fintech trade press, country tag index
why_relevant: Dedicated country landing page aggregating all Slovakia-tagged banking-technology stories — a ready-made pointer index for core-banking deals, fundings and vendor selections involving SK institutions.

Payments-specific global trade hub (news, interviews, country/market reports). Useful for SK acquiring, PSP, instant-payments and digital-euro items and for its vendor-mapping reports; note the site migrated from thepaypers.com/news structure, so historical links may redirect.

source_name: SITA Slovenska tlacova agentura — sita.sk / Webnoviny + PRservis / voFinanciach
why_relevant: National news agency; runs company/institution tag pages (e.g. /firmy-institucie/tatra-banka/) that aggregate every agency item about a given bank, plus PRservis.sk (verbatim corporate press releases) and voFinanciach.sk. Agency copy is what most SK media republish, so it is the upstream original for vendor/bank announcements.

source_name: Vendor press-clipping archives ('Napisali o nas') — e.g. Asseco Central Europe
why_relevant: Integrators republish the trade-press articles that name them — the fastest way to recover paywalled Trend/HN banking-IT coverage. Directly evidences the cell rationale: an archived piece titled 'Banky sa svojimi IT dodavatelmi nechvalia. Digitalne inovacie rady prezentuju ako svoje dielo'. Same pattern applies to Soitron, PosAm, EEA and other SK integrators.

Secondary SK tech outlets that cover payments-adjacent consumer topics (digital euro rollout implications, bank foundation IT grants). Lower credibility but useful for volume/recency and for surfacing terms and actors to snowball.

Not in the original cell list but confirmed to do the exact investigative genre the cell needs: reporting on IT tenders halted by the Public Procurement Office (UVO) after IT-community criticism, incl. a EUR 9.8m remote qualified e-signature server platform explicitly modelled on bank login solutions. Relevant to eID/authentication vendors serving banks.

Largest Slovak job portal and the de-facto default channel for bank and integrator IT vacancies. Its full-text parameter search_anywhere=<term> searches the whole ad body, so platform names (Temenos, Way4, ISO 8583) and Slovak domain phrases ('platobne systemy', 'kartove systemy', 'jadrovy bankovy system') can be swept on a schedule. Verified live query for 'platobne systemy' returned named employers incl. Tatra banka (IT analyst for corporate banking) and DanubePay (IT analyst for payment solutions), i.e. it directly leaks which institutions are staffing payment work.

Sector-scoped listing giving the full population of banking vacancies without keyword bias; the right denominator for measuring hiring intensity per bank and for catching ads that describe a platform without naming it.

Each bank, integrator and vendor has a stable company page listing all its current ads. This is the cleanest per-actor monitoring unit: build a watchlist of C-codes for banks (Tatra banka, 365.bank, SLSP, VUB, CSOB) and IT suppliers (Deutsche Telekom IT Solutions Slovakia C31332, TITANS freelancers C137115) and track their stack keywords over time.

source_name: Služby zamestnanosti (MPSVR SR / ÚPSVaR) - statutory vacancy register
why_relevant: Official state vacancy portal that replaced ISTP; Slovak employers are legally required under the Employment Services Act to report vacancies with their characteristics. That legal duty makes it the most complete and least commercially filtered vacancy corpus in SK - useful for catching bank/vendor roles never advertised on Profesia, and as a public-sector-grade cross-check.

Second-largest Slovak career site; carries IT consultant and IT support roles from employers that do not always post on Profesia, plus company-scoped listing pages (e.g. Slovensko IT a.s., the state IT company that runs public-sector fintech-adjacent projects).

Aggregates job ads from across the Slovak web, so a single query surfaces which portals and career pages a given bank or vendor is actually using - a cheap discovery layer for new sources. Operated by TREXIMA, which also produces Slovak labour-market analytics, giving a route to skills-taxonomy data.

Job database of the SME news portal; free posting for employers means a different employer spectrum than Profesia - notably smaller integrators, contractors and subcontractors that staff bank projects but do not pay for premium listings.

source_name: TITANS freelancers - IT contractor project marketplace (join.titans.eu)
why_relevant: The single highest-signal contractor source in this cell. Slovak market leader in IT freelancer outsourcing (founded 2013, 300+ clients, 1100+ placed freelancers, 45+ new projects/month). Its listings are project-shaped, not role-shaped: they state the client sector, the duration and the platform, e.g. an observed 'Mobile [Banking] architekt - Bratislava na 6 mesiacov' and 'IT biznis analytik - Bratislava na 12 mesiacov'. Contract length and start date are a direct proxy for a bank programme's phase and budget.

source_name: Tatra banka / Raiffeisen SK careers portal
why_relevant: First-party career portal of one of the two most IT-forward SK banks. Ads here are longer and more technical than the portal syndication and are the primary place a core-banking or payments migration would be named. Cross-check against the bank's Profesia page to catch ads posted in only one channel.

Largest SK bank (Erste group), explicitly positions itself as 'a modern IT company' in its own career copy, meaning it hires engineering roles in-house and describes stack in the ads. Also a confirmed live poster of card/fraud roles (a 'Card Fraud Specialist / Specialista klientskej bezpecnosti - kartove podvody' ad was observed via Profesia), which indexes card-platform and fraud-tooling activity.

Second-largest SK bank (Intesa Sanpaolo group). Group-owned banks tend to hire for integration and migration toward a parent-group platform, so VUB ads are the best early indicator of Intesa-driven core/payments consolidation reaching Slovakia.

KBC-group bank; completes the top-4 SK bank career-page set needed for comparable per-bank hiring baselines. Group IT centralisation means local ads reveal what is retained locally vs pulled to the group hub.

365.bank is the digital-first successor to Postova banka and the most likely SK institution to run a modern/cloud core (Mambu-class) or a heavy digital-channel rebuild; its hiring text is the cheapest read on that. The company_id filter gives a stable per-actor feed.

source_name: DanubePay a.s. - card processor hiring (observed via Profesia)
why_relevant: DanubePay is a Slovak card-processing/acquiring processor and was surfaced live hiring an 'IT analytik / IT analyticka pre oblast platobnych rieseni'. Processors sit between banks and schemes, so their vacancies expose switch/authorisation platform work and which bank clients they are scaling for - exactly the private-procurement proxy this cell targets.

source_name: Deutsche Telekom IT Solutions Slovakia - open positions
why_relevant: One of the largest IT employers in Slovakia (Kosice, Zilina, Banska Bystrica, Bratislava) and a nearshore delivery hub whose vacancies name client-project technologies. Useful for spotting delivery capacity being built for banking/payments accounts and for skills-supply baselining in eastern Slovakia. Also has a SmartRecruiters-hosted ATS feed.

source_name: SmartRecruiters / ATS-hosted career feeds used by SK employers
why_relevant: Slovak banks and integrators mostly do not build their own job engines - they embed an ATS (SmartRecruiters, SuccessFactors, Taleo, Workday, Recruitee). Identifying which ATS each actor uses converts a fragile HTML scrape into a stable, paginated, often JSON-backed feed, and lets one collector serve many actors.

source_name: LinkedIn - Slovakia company pages and job listings (sk.linkedin.com)
why_relevant: The only source in this cell that supports title mining on people, not just ads: counting 'Temenos consultant', 'Way4', 'BASE24' or 'ATM software' titles at SK-located employers reveals installed-base and delivery capacity even when no vacancy is open. Company pages are partially readable without login; the jobs search and people search are gated.

Cross-portal aggregator with high SEO reach; useful for retrospective discovery (finding an ad after it has been rotated off the original portal) and for enumerating which employers post banking roles at all. Aggregated copies must be traced back to the original posting before being treated as evidence.
